title: Telegram Now Has 1 Billion Users. Telebiz Just Built The First Real Business Layer On Top Of It
partialText:
Telegram now has one billion monthly active users. The share of crypto founders, funds, and remote-first teams who run their actual business inside it — deal flow, partnerships, hiring, follow-ups — has quietly become a majority. What none of them have is a business layer built for that reality. Tel Aviv startup Telebiz launches today with a wager that this is the largest under-served software surface in the industry, and that the way to serve it is to rebuild Telegram itself into a full business operating system — deals linked to chats, follow-ups scheduled, CRMs synced, and a native AI agent that drafts, summarizes, and chases stalled deals from inside the conversation window. The differentiator isn't the feature list; it's the architecture: Telebiz never stores or accesses Telegram messages, the client is open-source and publicly auditable, and AI requests travel browser-to-model under the user's own API key. Launch customers span the ETH restaking stack (ether.fi, $5.6B TVL), infrastructure (GenLayer), and venture (Collider Ventures). This is the beginning of a category — Telegram-native business software — that will get crowded fast, and Telebiz has picked the sharpest architectural bet in it.

What is Telebiz? Telebiz is a Tel Aviv-based software platform, launched July 9, 2026, that turns Telegram into a business operating system. It replaces the standard Telegram Web client with a version that adds CRM features — link chats to deals and contacts, schedule follow-ups, sync activity with HubSpot and Pipedrive — plus a built-in AI agent that drafts replies in the user's tone, summarizes group chats, surfaces leads across conversations, and follows up on stalled deals. The platform is designed for teams that run their business inside Telegram, particularly crypto startups, venture funds, and remote-first organizations. Its architecture is privacy-first: Telebiz servers never store or access Telegram messages (the device connects directly to Telegram), AI requests go browser-to-model provider under the user's own key, stored metadata is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, authentication is passwordless via Telegram, and the entire client is open-source.

What is Telebiz? Telebiz is a business operating system that runs inside Telegram, launched July 9, 2026 by a Tel Aviv-based team. It replaces the standard Telegram Web client with a version that adds CRM features, follow-up management, HubSpot and Pipedrive sync, and an in-chat AI agent that drafts replies, summarizes group chats, and chases stalled deals.

How is Telebiz different from other Telegram CRMs like CRMChat or Dise? Telebiz is a full replacement for Telegram Web (not a sidebar, extension, or bot connector), never stores or accesses Telegram messages, is open-source and publicly auditable, and uses a bring-your-own-model architecture for AI (user's own API key, user's chosen provider). Incumbents like CRMChat and Dise operate as external platforms or mini-apps that ingest Telegram data.

Does Telebiz see or store my Telegram messages? No. The user's device connects directly to Telegram's servers, exactly as the native Telegram Web client does. Telebiz servers only hold encrypted metadata (deal tags, contact labels, reminders) using AES-256-GCM. AI requests travel from the user's browser directly to the chosen model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) under the user's own API key.

Which CRMs does Telebiz sync with? At launch, Telebiz syncs with HubSpot and Pipedrive. Additional integrations are on the roadmap.

Who is Telebiz for? Teams that run most of their business communication inside Telegram: crypto startups, venture funds, remote-first organizations, partnership and BD functions. Launch customers include ether.fi, GenLayer, and Collider Ventures.

How much does Telebiz cost? Pricing details will be published at launch. Note that the bring-your-own-model AI architecture means users pay their own AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) directly for inference costs.

Is Telebiz open-source? The Telebiz client is open-source and publicly auditable. This is a deliberate design decision to remove the trust question entirely — anyone can inspect what the client does with their data.

title: The 2030 Post-Algorithm Reset
partialText: This article argues that while AI may trigger widespread disruption in white-collar employment, the long-term outcome may not be economic collapse but a shift toward smaller, more localized economies centered on trust, community, entrepreneurship, and meaningful work. title: Where Context Lives in a Cascading Voice Agent — and Why the STT Layer Quietly Decides Your Accuracy
partialText: A cascading voice agent chains speech-to-text, an LLM, and text-to-speech — and every layer downstream can only react to the transcript it's handed. title: AI Made Marketing Bland. Creativity Is the Moat Now, Says WalletConnect's Dayana Aleksandrova
partialText: AI was built to make us productive, not creative, argues Dayana Aleksandrova, Head of Social at WalletConnect. That's why marketing everywhere looks identical: people copy because copying feels safe, and AI made it effortless. Her fix is counterintuitive. Skip the polished positioning statement and lean into what's relatable: mundane facts, hyper-narrow obsessions, and the posts that feel slightly embarrassing to publish. She bans AI from her writing entirely, keeps it for video editing and productivity, and says the smallest move toward being unmistakable is owning one thing people instantly recognize as yours: a catchphrase, an aesthetic, a bald head that gets memed.
